scope: Three independently fitted rinkside standing-operator tripod installations; pitch interval below is a first-shot working interval.

source_evidence.drawing_readout: The front elevation gives approximately 6 cm from the camera base to lens-axis height by drawing proportion, not an explicitly dimensioned Sony optical-centre measurement. Add the actual mounting plate/head arrangement with a deliberately broad margin.
source_evidence.actual_image_findings: Compact body, monitor/support and head assembly on an upright tripod beside the board; standing operator. The lower legs and operator floor are occluded; no exact height, axis separation or entrance-pupil position is measured.
source_evidence.mechanical_reference_limit: The Ostrava photo shows an accessory platform and fluid head; it supports allowing mounting-stack height, but is not an Ankara placement measurement or proof of identical head hardware.

definitions.tilt_axis_reference: Q: closest point on the head's tilt axis to its pan axis. This is the centre about which the camera nods up/down, not the tripod feet or front lens glass.
definitions.pan_axis_reference: P: corresponding closest point on the pan axis. P and Q are geometric axis references, not two independently identified screws or bearings. Height is represented once by P; there is no additional free axial height from a physical base to Q.
definitions.offset_frame: Camera local x=right, y=down, z=forward. Read dimensions with the camera level; these axes rotate with the body.
definitions.reference_projection_centre: C0 at selected reference focal length. Its precise position is unknown and fitted.
definitions.complete_offset: R*(C-Q)=d+[0,0,pupil(z)]. The forward interval applies to this sum throughout the shot including row exposures; a bound on d alone is insufficient.
definitions.axis_spacing: Signed shortest distance between the two axis lines; it is not the vertical height of the head. Axes can intersect with a=0 while the camera lever remains nonzero.
definitions.height_gauge: For a vertical pan axis, P and Q are at the same height. With a <= 5 cm in magnitude and pan-axis tilt <= 3 degrees, their derived world-height difference is <= 2.62 mm. This is a geometric consequence, not a new fit parameter.
definitions.retracted_proposal: The assistant's proposal to fit a separate physical-base height and a free base-to-tilt axial height was incorrect: P_base + H*n is exactly redundant. No such parameter was added. Keep the existing 27/31-dimensional native chart.

tilt_axis_height_above_operator_floor_m.basis: Standing-operator event image and earlier rough head-height estimate, widened by the assistant. Each installation independent.

floor_to_ice_offset.application: Include this provisional uncertainty allowance in the single ice-relative Pz interval below. Do not add an independently fitted floor height or head-base height that can cancel Pz. Review the allowance if new floor evidence conflicts with it.

single_pan_reference_height_above_ice_m.basis: Assistant engineering working envelope: 1.2 to 1.8 m head height above operator floor, widened by a provisional +/-0.2 m floor-to-ice uncertainty allowance. This directly bounds the one existing Pz coordinate; neither component creates another fitted height. Not a surveyed interval.

complete_tilt_axis_to_projection_centre_.plain_language_cm: Left/right +/-5; upward 8 to 25; forward -10 to +30 including zoom. All components remain fitted.
complete_tilt_axis_to_projection_centre_.basis: Sony body drawing, compact event assembly and allowance for the accessory platform, sliding plate and unknown equivalent pupil. This is a broad working range, not a measured hardware boundary.

axis_spacing_m.basis: Compact fluid-head geometry; allow either sign and intersecting axes. Exact head model and spacing are not identified.

zoom_pupil_shift_from_reference_m.basis: Assistant provisional compact-optics allowance only. Sony publishes no entrance-pupil curve here. Fit both coefficients and constrain the resulting displacement over the actual continuous zoom range, together with the complete forward offset.

pan_axis_angle_from_vertical_degrees.basis: Upright levelled tripod seen in the event image; small levelling error remains fitted. This is not a measured three-degree tolerance.

tilt_axis_angle_from_camera_right_degree.basis: Camera seated normally on a tilt head with alignment and mounting uncertainty. Axis direction sign is a convention.

first_shot_optical_axis_elevation_degree.basis: Rinkside following of skater/ice; negative means down. Apply to the actual optical direction, not a raw Euler-angle chart.

first_shot_body_roll_degrees.basis: Upright body and near-level broadcast framing; not a command to freeze roll at zero.
